correctness.rationale: For any integer-valued CDF the mass on [a,b] is F(b)-F(a-1). The source divides each inclusive marginal PMF by F(b)-F(a), whose difference is the strictly positive p(a). Telescoping gives total mass product_i(1+p_i(a_i)/D_i)>1; replacing denominators by F(b)-F(a-1) proves the corrected law. The Brownian range cells have positive mass by full Wiener support; Brownian scaling and the reflection-principle bound yield exponential high-frequency inflation. Independent replay of the source series on its own applied bounds reproduces total mass 86.73217895307023, one atom 65.76516690845772, and the corrected conditional atom 0.75825567514039.

originality.rationale: The general integer-inclusive normalization identity is known and is not claimed as novel. New is the source-specific failure of the 2026 Wiener-range Eq. value.rationale: The defective quantity is the central constrained discrete market law, not a peripheral typographical symbol. Its two-coordinate PMF sums to 86.732 instead of 1 for the article’s own reported bounds and even assigns 65.765 to a single cell, making probability/risk estimates invalid as printed. Moreover, Brownian short-time scaling shows the error is unbounded and at least exponential in reciprocal sampling interval, directly targeting the high-frequency regime emphasized by the source. The corrected exact conditional model restores admissible risk probabilities without changing the untruncated construction.
